one_line: Governed evidence workbench for auditable human-agent delivery workflows.
what_it_does: Shares a deliverable contract, criterion-linked evidence, deterministic coverage checks, and a human-controlled release boundary between a person and browser agent.
leverage_rationale: Typed evidence and authority boundaries are central to the product; a general UI-driving agent could not comparably provide the same reliable, auditable shared state without substantial friction.
leverage_evidence: Five narrow WebMCP tools operate on the shared evidence workspace and audit ledger.
Agent can prepare a passing package but cannot approve or release it.
execution_rationale: The dark workspace is coherent and purpose-built, with visible evidence/status progression, though the stills do not make every end-to-end step legible.
execution_evidence: Three video frame sheets show changing evidence/workflow states and status cards.
Devpost packaging describes deterministic PASS and AWAITING_HUMAN_REVIEW states.
impact_rationale: High-consequence teams have a real need for traceable evidence and controlled release; the workflow directly addresses trust and auditability.
impact_evidence: Product is explicitly designed around evidence coverage, acceptance criteria, and human release control.
Shared contract and audit history address a concrete governance problem.
creativity_rationale: The combination of evidence workbench, deterministic gate, and human-only release is a fresh, ambitious application of WebMCP.
creativity_evidence: Agent and human share one auditable deliverable workflow rather than a generic chat or button proxy.
Authority boundaries are modeled as product behavior.
usability_note: Purposeful but dense evidence UI; likely usable for its professional audience.
red_flags: Tool-call labels are not clearly readable in the supplied frame sheets.
advance_reason: Strong WebMCP-specific governance workflow with credible product and video evidence.

one_line: Evidence-preserving human observation layer for agent reasoning.
what_it_does: Captures natural-language observations, confirms the source, separates hypotheses from facts, and exposes traceable memory to agents through WebMCP.
leverage_rationale: The structured epistemic boundary and queryable confirmed memory materially improve agent reliability over scraping or importing notes, although the underlying capture workflow remains possible without WebMCP.
leverage_evidence: Original human evidence is preserved before semantic construction.
Relations are classified by support level instead of silently becoming facts.
execution_rationale: The light card-based product is coherent and shows populated evidence/media states, but explicit agent execution is only partially visible.
execution_evidence: Frame sheets show distinct input, evidence, and structured-result states.
Visible cards and media support a concrete observation-to-memory workflow.
impact_rationale: People and teams need durable context that agents can use without confusing inference with observation; the use case is broad and credible.
impact_evidence: Product addresses loss of unstructured human context and provenance of AI interpretation.
Natural-language capture lowers the burden of recording observations.
creativity_rationale: The explicit human-evidence/agent-reasoning split and epistemic classification model are notably original and deeply pursued.
creativity_evidence: Two-stage semantic discovery and epistemic classification.
Unknown information is intentionally left unknown.
usability_note: Natural-language entry and card-based review suggest approachable use.
red_flags: Explicit WebMCP calls are not legible in the supplied stills.
standouts: Human context to confirmed memory pipeline
advance_reason: Original, high-value memory/provenance concept with credible visible product states.

one_line: Open-source ERP where agents draft and query while humans approve irreversible accounting actions.
what_it_does: Lets an agent query reports and shared ERP state, create editable drafts, and pause before human approval of commits.
leverage_rationale: Typed tools expose live ERP state and structured drafts while preserving human authority over bookkeeping; generic UI driving is markedly less reliable and safe.
leverage_evidence: Agent queries real ledger/report data without scraping.
draft_quote and get_current_view share an editable live draft; submit_draft suspends to human approval.
execution_rationale: This is the clearest end-to-end demonstration: activity progresses through named tools, returned data, and coherent ERP states.
execution_evidence: Frame sheets visibly show agent activity, tool-like operations, statuses, and returned data.
Visible operations include report/dashboard/product queries and result panels.
impact_rationale: SMEs have real operational, accounting, tax, and payroll needs; safer agent assistance in an ERP directly addresses consequential workflow friction.
impact_evidence: Scope covers quotes, orders, shipping, accounting, invoicing, VAT, and HR/payroll.
Human approval protects the irreversible bookkeeping boundary.
creativity_rationale: Applying shared-screen WebMCP collaboration and structured approval to a full ERP is ambitious and memorable.
creativity_evidence: One draft, two editors model.
Approval is enforced by structured tool boundary rather than only a UI warning.
usability_note: Dense ERP surface is appropriate to the domain; shared activity improves inspectability.
advance_reason: Exceptional WebMCP leverage and unusually clear execution evidence in a consequential domain.

one_line: Shared human-agent workspace with auditable proposals and human-only consequential decisions.
what_it_does: Agents read, analyze, compare, and mutate workspace tasks, then prepare decisions that a human must resolve before state changes.
leverage_rationale: The domain-layer decision invariant and shared structured state make WebMCP central to safe collaboration, beyond a browser automation convenience.
leverage_evidence: Six tools span reading, mutation, proposal, and human-only resolution.
Agent attempts at resolve_decision are rejected without mutation.
execution_rationale: The product is coherent and visibly demonstrates the agent reaching a blocked decision boundary; post-approval completion is not shown.
execution_evidence: Frames show agent activity and an explicit blocked/human decision state.
Description states rejection preserves workspace state and UI approval records the chain.
impact_rationale: Teams increasingly need agents to do useful analysis without silently committing consequential changes; this directly serves that need.
impact_evidence: Decision Ledger records the resulting chain.
Human approval controls consequential workspace changes.
creativity_rationale: A layered capability model and domain-enforced authority boundary are a strong, practical interaction design for human-agent work.
creativity_evidence: Blocked agent action is treated as a first-class product state.
Same domain operations power UI and WebMCP.
usability_note: Clear approval state and auditable activity support confident use.
red_flags: Frames show the blocked boundary more clearly than successful approval completion.
advance_reason: Strong safety-centered agent workspace with direct evidence of the core boundary.

one_line: Agent-built playable lessons that turn learner actions into evidence of understanding.
what_it_does: Takes a learning brief, has an agent create and validate a playable game, then records learner predictions, attempts, corrections, hints, and mastery.
leverage_rationale: The agent is not merely filling UI controls: it generates, playtests, diagnoses, and iterates a bespoke learning game, while WebMCP provides structured access to the canvas and diagnostics.
leverage_evidence: Agent creates complete HTML/CSS/JS games from natural-language goals.
Agent can playtest, inspect runtime diagnostics and learning evidence, and improve the draft.
execution_rationale: Branded, coherent screens show setup and populated evidence states, though the stills do not clearly expose the full tool-call chain.
execution_evidence: Frame sheets show distinct setup, game/evidence, and populated record states.
Product flow is visibly more than a static quiz.
impact_rationale: Teachers, parents, and trainers have a real need for adaptive, experiential learning; playable demonstrations can reveal understanding better than answer selection.
impact_evidence: Targets learner-specific goals and contexts.
Records behavioral evidence such as experiments, revisions, and demonstrated mastery.
creativity_rationale: Turning agent generation into a playable lesson and using play behavior as assessment is a genuinely fresh interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Natural-language brief becomes a functioning browser game.
Learning evidence is collected through exploration and mistakes.
usability_note: Strong branding and concrete game output make the concept approachable.
red_flags: Tool names and complete agent iteration are not legible in the stills.
advance_reason: High-impact educational concept with unusually ambitious agent-generated interaction.

one_line: Local-first runtime where humans and agents build and use custom information systems from an app spec.
what_it_does: Composes types, fields, views, forms, widgets, and rules into local SQLite-backed apps, exposing both builder tools and dynamically generated app tools.
leverage_rationale: Dynamic tools generated from the live app spec let an agent build capabilities and immediately use them; this shared canonical artifact is substantially beyond UI automation.
leverage_evidence: Fixed builder tools shape the application itself.
Application tools are generated dynamically from the live specification.
execution_rationale: Frames show construction, configuration, and preview/result states, but pale small text limits verification of the complete loop.
execution_evidence: Frame sheets show changing cards, forms, configuration panels, and previews.
Packet states the complete loop is build, generate capabilities, use, and evolve.
impact_rationale: Small teams and individuals can create tailored information systems without committing to a fixed SaaS workflow; local-first persistence adds practical value.
impact_evidence: Reusable primitives target custom information-system creation.
Browser-local SQLite/OPFS persistence supports local-first use.
creativity_rationale: Treating the application specification as the canonical artifact and regenerating the agent surface as the app evolves is highly original and ambitious.
creativity_evidence: Build and use are one continuous agent-human loop.
Tool surface changes with the live app spec without abandoning ordinary data operations.
usability_note: Powerful but configuration-dense; clarity is harder to assess from the light screenshots.
red_flags: Small, pale frame content makes tool calls and outputs difficult to verify.
advance_reason: Ambitious agent-native runtime with strong leverage and originality, despite moderate execution legibility.

one_line: Shared AI-human stock screening and research canvas with stable results and live charts.
what_it_does: Defines typed screeners, runs them against market data, pins results, and turns rows into visible chart panels that either human or agent can rearrange.
leverage_rationale: Structured screener definitions, stable result sets, and shared canvas state substantially reduce copying and brittle UI manipulation, though a general agent could eventually perform similar research.
leverage_evidence: WebMCP tools operate on the same workspace document as the panel/grid UI.
Typed catalog validates universes, fields, and operators.
execution_rationale: The financial dashboard is coherent and shows changing data panels and charts, with plausible research progression but limited readable tool evidence.
execution_evidence: Frame sheets show dark dashboard, tables/charts, and populated research states.
Packet describes backend screener evaluation over real OHLCV data.
impact_rationale: Investors and researchers have a clear need to iterate on hypotheses without repeatedly moving data between an agent and canvas.
impact_evidence: Product directly targets stock-price analysis and screener iteration.
Stable pinned results and live charts support hypothesis testing.
creativity_rationale: A shared editable research canvas is a fresh synthesis, though screening and charting are established categories.
creativity_evidence: Agent-created result rows become first-class rearrangeable panels.
Human and agent can define and inspect the same typed screener.
usability_note: Dashboard conventions fit the research audience; density is appropriate but requires orientation.
red_flags: No public repository is listed; implementation depth is judged from demo evidence and description.
advance_reason: Credible, useful financial research workflow with meaningful shared-state leverage.

one_line: Offline-first training journal where agents analyze history and safely evolve plans.
what_it_does: Separates planned, completed, and suggested training data, provides analysis and exports, and lets an agent prepare narrowly scoped drafts requiring human activation.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP removes a multi-step export/chat/import loop and provides focused read/write tools over live training state, while ordinary journaling remains possible without it.
leverage_evidence: 17-tool catalog exposes focused profile, history, progress, schedule, and draft/activation operations.
New programs are immutable drafts with an impact preview and explicit human confirmation.
execution_rationale: The product is visually polished and shows multiple coherent journal/workflow states; direct tool execution is not clearly readable.
execution_evidence: Frame sheets show branded landing, prompts, cards, and populated journal states.
Packet describes offline PWA, charts, exports, and draft activation flow.
impact_rationale: Athletes need reliable records and safe plan adaptation; separating facts from suggestions and preserving control addresses a real health/training problem.
impact_evidence: Supports strength and swimming history, sessions, substitutions, discomfort, wellbeing, and progression.
Offline-first and portable exports support continuity and ownership of personal data.
creativity_rationale: The offline, provenance-aware training journal plus constrained agent planning is a thoughtful and ambitious synthesis.
creativity_evidence: Planned work, completed facts, and future suggestions remain separate.
Agent-assisted plan changes are staged and human-confirmed.
usability_note: Mobile-first visual system and staged changes suggest strong usability for athletes.
red_flags: Authenticated assistant flow and tool calls are not directly legible in supplied stills.
advance_reason: Polished, high-value training workflow with meaningful WebMCP reduction in friction.

one_line: Fantasy football squad builder where an agent compares futures and applies a winning plan atomically.
what_it_does: Uses seeded probabilistic scenarios, formations, player outlooks, and budget-constrained upgrades to compare and commit fantasy XI plans.
leverage_rationale: The agent gets capability unavailable as ordinary UI forms—multi-scenario simulation, deterministic probability, and atomic application—making WebMCP central to the experience.
leverage_evidence: Six tools have no button, including simulate_scenarios and atomic apply_scenario.
Tools answer probability and outlook questions rather than merely reproducing visible counts.
execution_rationale: The frames clearly progress through player comparisons and a concrete lineup/field result; the workflow is easy to understand and visually strong.
execution_evidence: Frame sheets show changing player/data panels and an assembled field lineup.
Demo concept produces a specific roster arrangement from comparison activity.
impact_rationale: Fantasy Premier League players have a real recurring optimization and planning need; the tool provides useful decision support and saves complex comparison effort.
impact_evidence: Budget, rotation risk, club correlation, formations, and projected points address actual fantasy decisions.
Atomic plan application reduces error when changing a squad.
creativity_rationale: An agent-only scenario simulation and atomic plan interaction is a memorable, original extension of fantasy squad building.
creativity_evidence: No UI form offers the same multi-future comparison interaction.
Seeded Monte Carlo creates reproducible comparisons.
usability_note: Strong visual football-field result, though the data-dense interface may take orientation.
red_flags: Tool labels are too small to verify individually in the stills.
advance_reason: Distinctive agent-native capability with clear, concrete output and strong evidence of execution.

one_line: WebMCP planner for Kurdish events, calendar conversions, and multi-time-zone coordination.
what_it_does: Finds real events, converts dates across calendar systems, compares local times, opens the visible calendar, and stages an editable unsaved plan.
leverage_rationale: Structured event records, calendar conversions, and time-zone comparisons remove brittle scraping and manual reconstruction; the human retains final copy/share control.
leverage_evidence: Five schema-validated tools expose event, calendar, and time-zone capabilities.
UI-affecting tools update the same visible calendar and only stage a private draft.
execution_rationale: The dark calendar UI shows event/planning state changes and a plausible workflow, but the stills are dense and do not expose tool calls clearly.
execution_evidence: Frame sheets show calendar/event views and populated planning panels.
Packet specifies a coherent Nawroz planning flow ending in an editable unsaved draft.
impact_rationale: Diaspora families and communities have a specific, underserved coordination problem across calendars and time zones; the workflow directly addresses it.
impact_evidence: Supports Gregorian, Kurdish Bashur, Kurdish Rojhalat, Persian, and Hijri conversions.
Compares Erbil, London, Toronto, and other IANA time zones for one event plan.
creativity_rationale: The culturally specific calendar and time-zone collaboration model is original and meaningfully pursued rather than cosmetic localization.
creativity_evidence: Nawroz planning combines event discovery, multi-calendar conversion, and multi-city timing.
Agent research is paired with human-verifiable visible calendar state.
usability_note: Useful workflow, though the dense dark presentation may require refinement for broad family use.
red_flags: Execution and tool invocation are difficult to verify from small dark frame sheets.
advance_reason: Strong niche impact and meaningful structured calendar leverage despite moderate evidence legibility.
